Pakistan Bar Council (Recognition Of Universities) Rules 2005
Pakistan Bar Council (Recognition Of Universities)
Rules 2005
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II, 31st December, 2005]
S.R.O.1306(I)/2005, dated
31-12-2005.---In exercise of powers conferred by sections 13(k) and 55(r) of
the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973 and all other enabling
provisions in this behalf, the Pakistan Bar Council hereby makes and notifies
the following "Pakistan Bar Council (Recognition of Universities) Rules,
2005".
CHAPTER I
Preliminary
1. (i) These Rules may be called
"Pakistan Bar Council (Recognition of Universities) Rules, 2005".
(ii) they shall
come into force at once.
2. In these rules unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject or context:
(a)
"Act" means the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973 (Act
No. XXXV of 1973).
(b) "Section"
means a section of the Act.
(c) "Council"
means the Pakistan Bar Council.
(d) "Committee"
means Legal Education Committee of the Pakistan Bar Council.
(e)
"University" means University established by law in Pakistan
and/or outside Pakistan
awarding Bachelor degree in law.
(f) "Degree
awarding Institution" means such Institution not designated as University
but authorized to award Bachelor's degree in Law under a statute or a charter.
(g) "Recognized
degree" means and includes a Bachelor's degree in law awarded by a
University or a Degree awarding Institution recognized by the Pakistan Bar
Council.
(h) "Standard
of Education" includes physical factors like premises spread over about 10,000 square yards, a Law
faculty of qualified and experienced teachers and library composed of at least
20,000 volumes.
CHAPTER 2
Recognition of
Universities and Degree Awarding Institutions
3. The Universities and Degree
awarding Institutions in Pakistan
or outside Pakistan
listed in First Schedule have been recognized by the Council for the purpose of
recognition of their Bachelor's degrees in law.
4. The Universities or Degree
Awarding Institutions in Pakistan
or outside Pakistan
awarding Bachelor's degree in law which are recognized after the framing of
these rules shall be listed in the Second Schedule.
5. (i) Any University or Degree
Awarding Institution not recognized by the Council may apply to the Council for
recognition in the prescribed form mentioned under third schedule, accompanied
by a fee of Rs.100,000 (Rupees One hundred thousand only):
Provided that Rs.25,000 (Rupees
twenty Five thousand only) out of the application fee shall be non-refundable
in the event of rejection of such application.
(ii) Any person obtaining
Bachelor's degree in law from a University not recognized by the Council may
apply for the recognition of his degree on the prescribed form mentioned in the
Fourth Schedule with a non-refundable fee
of Rs.5,000.
6. The Committee on receipt of such
application shall hold inquiry into the standard
and quality of education being imparted by applying University/Institution:
Provided that such application shall be decided
within reasonable period of time not exceeding six months.
CHAPTER 3
Inspection and Derecognition
7. (i) If the Committee at any
time after inspection is satisfied that a University and a Degree
Awarding Institution in Pakistan
recognized by the Council is imparting substandard education, it may, after due
enquiry, recommend derecognition of such University or Degree Awarding
Institution to the Council.
(ii) The Council after receipt of
such recommendation and after giving
opportunity of hearing, may derecognize such University or Degree
Awarding Institution and order deletion of its name from the First or Second
Schedule as the case may be.
(iii) The Council or the
Committee may, as the case may be, associate any member of a Provincial Bar
Council during the course of any inspection
or inquiry.

or degree awarding
